import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`seamless-auth-admin-dashboard` is the operator-facing application for managing and observing a
Seamless Auth deployment.

It is a separate React/Vite frontend built as static assets, not a hidden screen inside the auth
server. It talks to your application backend through the Seamless Auth server adapter, and the
adapter talks to the auth API.

---

## What It Is For

Use the dashboard when you need a UI for:

- browsing, creating, editing, and deleting users
- editing global user roles
- managing organizations and organization memberships
- tracking passkey enrollment and sending enrollment invites
- inspecting and revoking sessions
- preparing an account for device replacement
- reviewing auth events
- investigating suspicious activity
- checking dashboard metrics
- editing system configuration

It is the operational layer for your auth system.

---

## Main Areas

The dashboard defines these routes in `src/App.tsx`. Screens inside the operator shell require
admin read access:

| Route            | Screen                                                          |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/`              | Overview                                                        |
| `/users`         | Users                                                           |
| `/users/:id`     | User detail                                                     |
| `/organizations` | Organizations                                                   |
| `/enrollment`    | Passkey enrollment directory and invites                        |
| `/coverage`      | Authentication coverage report                                  |
| `/sessions`      | Sessions                                                        |
| `/events`        | Events                                                          |
| `/security`      | Security signals and the audit trail panel                      |
| `/system`        | System configuration                                            |
| `/profile`       | Profile                                                         |

Public routes handle sign-in and redirects:

| Route               | Purpose                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/login`            | Dashboard sign-in (passkey, magic link, OTP, and OAuth flows) |
| `/verify-magiclink` | Magic link verification                                       |
| `/oauth/callback`   | OAuth provider callback                                       |
| `/unauthenticated`  | Landing screen for signed-out or non-admin users              |

<Aside type="note">
  Maturity varies by screen. Enrollment shipped in dashboard `v0.8.0`. The Coverage page, the
  Security audit trail panel, and the "Phishing-resistant only" setting are on `main` but not yet
  in a tagged release. `seamless-cli` and the auth API image currently pin dashboard `v0.7.0`,
  which has none of these.
</Aside>

---

## Access Model

The dashboard uses `@seamless-auth/react` and every data call goes through the server adapter:

```txt
dashboard  ->  <API_URL>/auth/*  ->  server adapter  ->  Seamless Auth API
```

The adapter reads the dashboard's session cookie and forwards a bearer token upstream. Point the
dashboard at the origin that mounts the adapter at `/auth`, normally your own application backend.
Pointing it at the Seamless Auth API directly does not work, because the API does not serve the
`/auth` prefix.

Dashboard access is based on scoped admin roles:

| Role          | Dashboard meaning                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `admin`       | Broad legacy admin access               |
| `admin:read`  | Can read admin screens and data         |
| `admin:write` | Can perform write actions and also read |

Route access is gated on `admin:read` and write controls on `admin:write`. Both checks run in the
browser for user experience only; the auth API is the enforcement point for every request.

Sensitive writes require fresh step-up authentication, including user create, edit, and delete,
session revocation, device-replacement recovery, OAuth provider changes, and audit trail export.
The dashboard tries a passkey first and falls back to TOTP when the account has it enabled.

---

## Operational Workflows

### Users

The users area supports user search, user creation, user detail review, role edits, session
review and revocation, credential review, anomaly context, and user deletion.

### Organizations

The organizations area uses `/admin/organizations/*` routes to create and delete organizations,
edit names and slugs, list members, and add, update, or remove members with roles and scopes.

### Enrollment

The enrollment area uses `/admin/enrollment` to filter users by organization, passkey enrollment
status, and how they were added, and `/admin/enrollment/invites` to invite users who still need a
passkey. Sending invites requires `admin:write`.

### Coverage

The coverage area reads `/admin/reports/authentication-coverage`. It shows how many users hold a
phishing-resistant credential, overall and by organization, with a trend, the authenticator mix,
the sign-in mix, and the enforced login policy. The report can be downloaded as CSV.

### Sessions

The sessions area uses `/admin/sessions` to list active sessions across users and
`/admin/sessions/by-id/:id` to revoke individual or selected sessions. The user detail page uses
`/admin/sessions/:userId/revoke-all` to revoke every session for one user.

### Device replacement recovery

The user detail page can call:

```http
POST /admin/users/:userId/recovery/device-replacement
```

That route requires `admin:write` access and fresh step-up authentication. The request must record
identity proofing (`in_person` or `remote_exception`, an evidence reference such as a ticket
number, and a named approver for a remote exception). Revoking sessions, removing passkeys, and
disabling TOTP credentials each default to on. The response returns counts only.

### Audit trail

The security area includes an audit trail panel. It runs the auth event hash chain check through
`/admin/auth-events/integrity` and exports a period of events as NDJSON through
`/admin/auth-events/export` after a fresh step-up.

### System configuration

The system configuration area reads and writes `/system-config/admin` and can update:

- app name
- available and default roles
- login methods, passkey fallback, and passkey enrollment prompts
- the "Phishing-resistant only" mode, which refuses every sign-in that is not a passkey
- OAuth provider configuration, through `/system-config/oauth-providers`
- access and refresh token TTLs
- rate limit and slowdown values
- lockout policy
- WebAuthn relying party ID and allowed origins
- authenticator policy (synced passkeys, attachment, user verification, attestation, and AAGUID
  allow and deny lists)

OAuth provider client secrets are referenced by env var name, not entered as raw secret values in
the dashboard. Changing the relying party ID invalidates passkeys registered against the old ID,
and the dashboard asks for confirmation before saving that change.

---

## Runtime Configuration Model

The dashboard is built as static assets and is designed for runtime config injection, so the same
built image can be pointed at different environments without a rebuild.

`src/lib/runtimeConfig.ts` resolves the API base in this order:

1. `window.__SEAMLESS_CONFIG__.API_URL`, from `/config.js`
2. the page's own origin, when built with `VITE_SAME_ORIGIN=true`
3. the baked `VITE_API_URL`

In the container image, `index.html` loads `/config.js`, and `entrypoint.sh` writes
`window.__SEAMLESS_CONFIG__` from the `API_URL` env var at startup. The entrypoint rejects a value
that does not start with `http://` or `https://`. The app throws on startup if no API URL resolves.

| Variable           | When it is read | Purpose                                                             |
| ------------------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `API_URL`          | Container start | Origin serving the server adapter, written into `config.js`         |
| `VITE_API_URL`     | Build time      | Baked API base for local development and the root build             |
| `VITE_SAME_ORIGIN` | Build time      | `true` derives the API base from `window.location.origin`           |
| `VITE_BASE_PATH`   | Build time      | Asset and router base path: `/` by default, `/console/` for console |

For local development, copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set `VITE_API_URL` to the origin that runs
your server adapter (`http://localhost:3000` in the example).

---

## Deployment Shape

You can use the dashboard in a few ways:

- run the official image, `ghcr.io/fells-code/seamless-auth-admin-dashboard`
- clone the source and customize it
- serve it at `/console` from your application API or an auth instance
- include it from `seamless-cli` during project setup

### Official image

The image is published to GHCR on each version tag (`vX.Y.Z`), and `latest` tracks the newest
version. Pin an explicit `vX.Y.Z` tag in production. The image serves the build through
unprivileged nginx on port `8080` and includes a health check at `/health`.

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 \
  -e API_URL=https://app.example.com \
  ghcr.io/fells-code/seamless-auth-admin-dashboard:v0.8.0
```

### Served at `/console`

`npm run build:console` sets `VITE_BASE_PATH=/console/` and `VITE_SAME_ORIGIN=true`, so the
dashboard runs under `/console` and calls its own origin. The auth API image bundles this build at
a pinned dashboard tag and serves it at `/console` unless `SERVE_ADMIN_DASHBOARD=false`. The
Seamless API templates reverse-proxy it from the auth server at `/console` when
`SERVE_ADMIN_CONSOLE=true`, so the dashboard shares the origin and cookie scope of `/auth`. A
Next.js App Router app does the same with `createSeamlessConsoleProxy` from `@seamless-auth/nextjs`
([Next.js: Admin Console](/build/nextjs#admin-console)).

### From `seamless-cli`

`seamless init` asks where the admin console is hosted, or takes `--admin=<mode>`:

| Mode     | Result                                                                  |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `api`    | Default. Your API serves the console at `http://localhost:3000/console`; a full-stack web app serves it at `http://localhost:5173/console` |
| `image`  | Separate `admin` container from the official image                      |
| `source` | Separate `admin` container built from source unpacked into `admin/`     |
| `none`   | No admin console                                                        |

The `image` and `source` modes pin the same dashboard tag.

For a full-stack template such as Next.js, seamless-cli 0.20.0 ([fells-code/seamless-cli#239](https://github.com/fells-code/seamless-cli/pull/239)) supports `api` and `none`. In
`api` mode the Next.js starter serves the console from its own origin through
`createSeamlessConsoleProxy` ([Next.js: Admin Console](/build/nextjs#admin-console)), switched on
by `SERVE_ADMIN_CONSOLE=true` in `web/.env`. `image` and `source` are refused: a dashboard container
on `:5174` would call the app's `/auth` cross-origin, which the Next.js route handler does not
allow. Earlier CLI releases offered only `none` for full-stack templates.

---

## Relationship To The Rest Of The Ecosystem

The dashboard sits on top of the same auth system the rest of the ecosystem uses.

It depends on:

- auth sessions being issued correctly
- the server adapter mounted at `/auth`
- scoped admin access
- admin routes under `/admin/*` and metrics routes under `/internal/*`
- system configuration routes under `/system-config/*`
- step-up routes under `/step-up/*` for sensitive writes

It does not replace the auth server. It visualizes and operates it.
